answer: That removes the entire premise of a template farm, which depends on one text serving many identities, and forces a separate echo derivation per key. Because the opal nonce is published only after close, the pulse audit can verify each derivation and a shared text is provable as copied. The three words are derived from a 113 bit value mixing the epoch seed with the identity key, so no two keys ever receive the same triple. That is 17 dollars per alias.
